stage: real within-tool proxy runs completed; integrated 2×2 incompatible; bug-yield question remains open
reason_to_test: Three source-audited methods optimize different guidance signals. Real within-tool tests show proxy behavior worth probing, but the key uncertainty is whether those gains correspond to distinct, reproducible logic bugs at equal cost.
observed_feasibility: On 10 short SQLancer seeds, 9/10 database pairs completed and QPG made 7.33 more NoREC checks on average; seed 4109 completed no database despite exit 0. SQLancer++ feedback on/off was indistinguishable for 10 three-database seeds, but a 20-database follow-up had more rate-derived successful query pairs with feedback on in all five tested seeds (+215,+221,+373,+277,+244). These are proxy outcomes, not confirmed bug yield. See docs/dbms_guidance_campaign.md.
competing_hypotheses: Validity feedback raises executable SQL yield, but plan guidance adds no distinct logic bugs at matched cost.
Plan guidance reaches distinct bug behaviors beyond the gain from valid SQL alone.
Apparent cross-paper bug-yield differences arise mainly from DBMS, oracle, budget, and deduplication choices.

next_action.title: Pre-register an equal-CPU-hour bug-yield and behavior-coverage phase
next_action.procedure: Keep the SQLancer/QPG and SQLancer++ feedback studies separate. Freeze a repeated-seed, equal-CPU-hour budget; log exact per-database valid SQL and plan/behavior signatures. Independently reproduce and root-cause-deduplicate any NoREC discrepancy, including zero-discovery runs. Compare each toggle only with its own pinned baseline.
next_action.budget: Use a small preregistered gate before any full agent campaign; stop or redesign if setup failures or missing exact counters prevent interpretation.
next_action.supports_if: A proxy gain survives matched CPU cost and reaches distinct reproducible behaviors or logic bugs.
next_action.weakens_if: The proxy gain disappears at equal CPU cost or produces no additional distinct behavior after independent triage.
next_action.prerequisite: The integrated 2×2 design is incompatible in the released code; see docs/sqlancerpp_compatibility_audit.md.

stop_rule: Stop any cross-method effect or interaction claim until a common implementation, DBMS revision, oracle, and budget are validated.

reason_to_test: Two source-audited agent benchmarks report a gap between valid tool calls and task success. The actionable uncertainty is which stage loses information under a fixed tool and token budget.
competing_hypotheses: Selecting the wrong tool or route explains a substantial share of failed tasks.
The main loss occurs after valid tool calls, when the agent integrates evidence and forms an answer.
The apparent gap is substantially driven by benchmark grading or task composition.

next_action.title: Instrument matched tasks and replay oracle tool routes
next_action.procedure: Pin a public task subset, a single model, tool inventory, and call/token limits. Log routing, schema validity, evidence returned, evidence use, and final answer. Replay a valid oracle route with the same answer procedure and budget to estimate how much route choice explains the failure.
next_action.budget: Begin with 20 auditable multi-source tasks; set the larger sample after checking task and grading reproducibility.
next_action.supports_if: Oracle-route replay raises final task success on previously failed cases without changing evidence or token budget.
next_action.weakens_if: Final task success remains low after route correction, pointing to evidence integration or answer verification instead.
next_action.prerequisite: Verify benchmark task files, license, grading code, and availability of reproducible tool responses.

stop_rule: Do not claim a routing intervention if the benchmark cannot separate tool choice from evidence use or if oracle replay changes the information budget.

reason_to_test: The reviewed studies disagree in ways consistent with their different program-equivalence checks. Repository-scale behavior and timeout-related misclassification remain directly testable.
competing_hypotheses: Bounded symbolic equivalence improves uncertainty calibration after accounting for checker cost and error.
Short-program benchmark structure or checker timeouts explain the apparent advantage.
Model, sampling, and correctness-oracle differences explain more of the cross-study contrast than the equivalence method.

next_action.title: Audit equivalence-checker errors on a held-out repair set
next_action.procedure: Pin the released checker and a repository-held-out code-repair set. Compare embedding, CodeBLEU, and bounded symbolic equivalence on the same generated candidate patches. Independently adjudicate a stratified set of checker agreements, disagreements, and timeouts before any risk-coverage claim.
next_action.budget: First measure checker timeouts and reviewer effort on a small frozen sample; set a full matched compute budget from that pilot.
next_action.supports_if: Symbolic clustering improves calibrated selective risk after including checker runtime and false-equivalence errors.
next_action.weakens_if: Timeout or false-equivalence rates erase the risk-coverage gain, or the gain does not transfer beyond the original short-program benchmark.
next_action.prerequisite: Audit released implementations, candidate-sampling protocol, repository benchmark license, and independent correctness labels.

stop_rule: Defer an effectiveness claim if equivalence errors cannot be independently measured or repository-level correctness has only weak test oracles.
